summary: This informational memo documents how IPv4 is supported on MAPOS version 1.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2176 describes how Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) datagrams travel over MAPOS version 1. MAPOS means Multiple Access Protocol over SONET/SDH. The memo also explains how nodes find a link address for an IP address.

questions: how does ip run over mapos
subtitle: How IPv4 packets and address resolution work over MAPOS version 1.

tldr.problem: IPv4 needs a defined way to travel over MAPOS and to map an IP destination to its MAPOS HDLC address.
tldr.mechanism: IPv4 datagrams are carried in MAPOS HDLC frames; MAPOS ARP resolves IP addresses to HDLC addresses, while UNARP clears stale cache mappings.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2176 is an Informational description of IPv4 over MAPOS version 1 and has been updated by RFC 5494.

today: RFC 2176 is an Informational memo published in June 1997 and has been updated by RFC 5494. It documents IPv4 support for MAPOS version 1.

sections.title: IPv4 on the MAPOS Link Layer
sections.content:
MAPOS is a link-layer protocol for multiple access over SONET/SDH links. Its HDLC-based frames can connect nodes through a frame switch, and this memo describes carrying IPv4 over MAPOS version 1.

The document covers two tasks: placing an IP datagram in a MAPOS frame and resolving IP addresses to HDLC addresses. It is informational and says it was not produced by an IETF working group.
sections.plainLanguage: MAPOS carries frames over SONET/SDH links. This memo explains how an IPv4 datagram fits into a MAPOS frame and how a node finds the destination's link address.

sections.title: Encapsulating an IP Datagram
sections.content:
An IPv4 datagram is placed in the information field of a MAPOS HDLC frame. The frame's protocol field is set to 0x0021.

The information field may contain from one to 65,280 octets, which the memo gives as the MAPOS MTU. A large MTU can reduce IP header-processing overhead, but fragmentation along a path may degrade performance; the RFC points to Path MTU Discovery as one way to address this.
sections.plainLanguage: The MAPOS frame marks its information as an IP datagram and carries the datagram inside it. The maximum information-field length is 65,280 octets, but fragmentation can affect performance.

sections.title: Resolving an IP Address to an HDLC Address
sections.content:
Each node keeps an ARP cache that maps destination IP addresses to 8-bit HDLC addresses. If the address is missing, the node broadcasts an ARP request containing the destination IP address; the node that owns it replies with its HDLC address, which is cached.

MAPOS ARP frames use protocol field 0xFE01. The ARP hardware address space is 25, the protocol address space for IP is 2048, and the request and response operation codes are 1 and 2.
sections.plainLanguage: Before sending an IP datagram, a node needs the destination's link address. It can ask all nodes who owns the IP address and store the reply.

sections.title: UNARP and Cache Maintenance
sections.content:
When a node detects that its port has come up, it MUST broadcast UNARP to clear a stale mapping left by a previous node on that switch port. UNARP uses operation code 23 and broadcast target addresses; the node sends three packets at 30-second intervals.

A receiver clears the sender's IP-to-HDLC cache entry only when the cached HDLC address differs from the address in UNARP. Implementations must remove outdated entries and immediately clear entries associated with a lost link.
sections.plainLanguage: When a port comes up, a clearing message tells other nodes to remove a stale address mapping if it points elsewhere. The sender repeats it three times, 30 seconds apart.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC's Security Considerations section says security issues are not discussed in the memo. It provides no security procedures for ARP or UNARP.

UNARP can cause a receiver to clear a cache entry under the conditions defined by the protocol, but the memo does not analyze how an implementation should authenticate such a packet.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo does not discuss security. It gives no method for checking that address requests or clearing messages are genuine.
